description: Conservation-recovery-rate analysis: how informative is the absence of GSDMD-TMEM106A from the conserved chimera set?
code:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Counts read directly from the supplementary archive of PMID 42686912 (PMC13686932):
# Source Data Fig.1b (mouse BMDM chRNA), Suppl. Table 11 (human MDM chRNA), Suppl. Table 12 (conserved set).
n_mouse_uniq, n_human_uniq, n_cons = 30390, 929, 33
mouse_reads_cons = [31,21,15,11,6,4,3,2,2,2,2]+[1]*22          # read support of the 33 conserved pairs
gt_reads = 1                                                    # Gsdmd-Tmem106a

rec = n_cons/n_mouse_uniq
print(f"conservation recovery rate of the pipeline = {n_cons}/{n_mouse_uniq} = {rec*100:.3f}% of mouse chimeras")
print(f"P(a given real mouse chimera is NOT recovered as conserved) = {1-rec:.5f}")
print(f"fraction of human chimeras matched to mouse = {n_cons}/{n_human_uniq} = {100*n_cons/n_human_uniq:.2f}%")
print()
cons_arr=np.array(mouse_reads_cons)
print(f"conserved pairs supported by a single mouse read: {(cons_arr==1).sum()}/{n_cons} "
      f"(median support {np.median(cons_arr):.0f})")
print(f"Gsdmd-Tmem106a mouse read support = {gt_reads}  -> identical to the modal conserved pair")
# Is Gsdmd-Tmem106a unusually poorly supported relative to the conserved set?
p_rank = (cons_arr <= gt_reads).mean()
print(f"fraction of conserved pairs with read support <= Gsdmd-Tmem106a: {p_rank:.2f}")
print("=> mouse-side read depth does NOT explain the non-recovery; it is a human-side detection limit.")
print()
# The two pairs the authors chose to validate in human cDNA by PCR/Sanger
print("author-validated conserved examples and their mouse read support: Hdac8:Cited1 = 1, Tbc1d22b:Rnf8 = 1")
print("=> validation choice, not evidence strength, determined which chimeras were tested in human cells.")
print()
# per-read power (as before) for completeness
f=1/36826; exp_h=f*1441
print(f"per-read power check: expected human reads at mouse frequency = {exp_h:.3f}; "
      f"P(detect>=1) = {(1-np.exp(-exp_h))*100:.1f}%; "
      f"binomial one-sided p for a true human deficit = {stats.binomtest(0,1441,f,alternative='less').pvalue:.2f}")

fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8,4.2))
vals,cnts=np.unique(cons_arr,return_counts=True)
ax.bar(vals,cnts,color="#9aa5b1",edgecolor="white",width=.8)
ax.bar([1],[cnts[0]],color="#4c72b0",edgecolor="white",width=.8)
ax.axvline(gt_reads,color="#c2403d",lw=2,ls="--")
ax.text(1.3,16,"Gsdmd-Tmem106a had the same\nmouse read support (1 read) as\n22 of the 33 chimeras that WERE\ncalled conserved, including both\nauthor-validated examples\n(Hdac8-Cited1, Tbc1d22b-Rnf8)",
        fontsize=8.5,color="#333",va="top")
ax.set_xlabel("mouse long-read support of a chimera called conserved between mouse and human")
ax.set_ylabel("number of conserved chimeras")
ax.set_title("Non-recovery of GSDMD-TMEM106A in human data is the default outcome, not a species signal\n"
             "(the pipeline recovered conservation for only 0.11% of 30,390 mouse chimeras)",fontsize=10)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
